children.text: Asynchronous I/O in DuckDB: Work, Thread, Work

TL;DR: Starting with v2.0, scheduled for fall 2026, DuckDB will support asynchronous reads of Parquet and CSV files. This can significantly speed up queries when synchronous I/O does not saturate the available bandwidth, as is typical in EC2/S3 compute-storage setups.

It doesn't matter how fast query operators are in a database system if we can't pull in the data quickly. For most of DuckDB's history, however, this problem was largely avoided by pruning data early. By pushing down filters and projections, we could ensure that we only read what we actually needed.

This worked particularly well because DuckDB primarily ran locally, with its main use case being as a quick-draw database engine for querying data directly from your machine's SSD. We could split the data into several partitions, such as row groups for Parquet files or fixed-size buffers for CSV files, and load them with low latency and high bandwidth. As a result, the main bottlenecks were elsewhere: subqueries, joins, aggregations, and so on. The actual data access path received less attention because synchronous access was perfectly suitable for this use case.
As usual, things changed. We realized that DuckDB's architecture was a great fit for querying remotely stored large-scale datasets, such as data lakes (e.g.,
, we can even run DuckDB as a server using the
. The original expectation of data files sitting on a local SSD therefore no longer always holds.

The practical implication of these changes is that many current DuckDB setups need to transfer files from remote storage to the machine that will actually process them. For data lakes, for example, a typical setup is to store the data in blob storage, such as S3, and process it on an EC2 machine in the same region. In this setup, latency and bandwidth play a much more significant role. If we cannot issue enough concurrent requests to use the available network bandwidth, performance can suffer drastically, with threads spending a large amount of their time waiting for remote reads instead of processing data.
As an example, let's consider a simple query over a remote Parquet file. For simplicity, let's assume we only have a single thread executing.

content_blocks.text: FROMread_parquet('s3://bucket/file.parquet');

children.text: A Parquet scan is partitioned into row-group-based jobs, with each job containing one or more fetch tasks that issue byte-range requests. With synchronous I/O, the worker thread will be blocked, waiting for the data to arrive at the machine before performing actual work, such as decoding, aggregating, and so on. You can see a visual depiction in the figure below, where the thread is blocked from doing any work while it waits for the read to finish.

content_blocks.alt: Synchronous read
Synchronous read

children.text: To address this, we have been implementing asynchronous I/O pipelines in DuckDB. They are currently implemented for Parquet and for uncompressed, seekable UTF-8 CSV files, with support for other formats, such as DuckDB's native format and JSON, still to come. In the remainder of this blog post, we will give a simple explanation of how asynchronous I/O is implemented in DuckDB and provide benchmarks for both Parquet and CSV files.
If you would like to try asynchronous I/O now, you can do so by using
. Asynchronous I/O will be used by default from the next major DuckDB version, v2.0, released

The conceptual idea of asynchronous I/O is rather simple: we should be able to start an I/O operation without blocking the worker thread that requested it. Applied to our Parquet example, the same picture would look like the following:

content_blocks.alt: Asynchronous read
Asynchronous read

children.text: In this example, we have two
threads and one regular worker thread. The

in flight while the worker thread decodes data. During the initial warm-up, the scan task parks, leaving the worker thread free to run other pipeline tasks. Once the first job is ready, fetching and decoding can overlap.
In DuckDB, we implemented something similar. We have

– This pool contains our worker threads (by default: one for each available CPU thread). These are the ones that do real work, like decoding, joins, and aggregations. They prioritize regular work but can also perform I/O tasks when idle.
– A pool of threads intended for asynchronous tasks, primarily blocking I/O.

The main reason we have these two different pools is that, for remote I/O, these threads can spend almost all their time blocked, waiting for an HTTP response, for example, and hence have very little CPU utilization. Because of that, we have many more
workers than system threads, with the default setting being
and the total being capped at 256.
It's of utmost importance to keep as many of our

threads busy as possible. To ensure that, we implement a read-ahead strategy instead of issuing reads on demand. This means scheduling fetch tasks ahead of what our regular worker threads currently need.

One thing we need to be attentive to is that read-ahead buys throughput by holding memory. If decoding is slow and the network is fast, prefetched data can accumulate and lead to out-of-memory issues. To mitigate this, we also implemented asynchronous memory governance. Both read-ahead and memory governance will be explained in more detail in the following sections.

The idea of read-ahead is also straightforward. Instead of starting a read at the exact moment a regular worker needs the data, we schedule fetch tasks for work that lies further ahead. While a regular worker decodes the current job, the ASYNC threads are already pulling in data for the next jobs. The goal is to keep enough fetch tasks in flight to hide the latency of remote storage.

The jobs are units of work that can be scheduled and processed independently, and they can be different depending on the underlying file format. For a Parquet file, a job is one row group of one file. For a CSV file, a job is a scan boundary that generally covers a fixed byte range within the file.

A Parquet job might be broken down into multiple fetch tasks depending on the query projections, filter pushdowns, physical column locations, and which nearby byte ranges can be combined. The two fetch tasks in the figure below are illustrative, as their exact grouping and sizes depend on the file and query.

For CSV files, we don't have the same granularity of information as we do for Parquet files. A job's fetch tasks load its starting buffer if it is not already in memory and, when the scan boundary reaches the end of that buffer, the following buffer as well (e.g., to handle lines that are split across two buffers).

content_blocks.alt: Jobs
Jobs

children.text: Filling the queue requires no dedicated producer thread. Any regular worker that comes looking for scan work first tops up the queue as far as it is allowed to. The limit is either given by a user-specified number of slots or by a memory budget. If there is space, a job and its fetch tasks are created. The fetch tasks are scheduled immediately on the
pool, while the job is admitted to the read-ahead queue in batch order.
threads execute individual fetch tasks independently of the job queue's claim order. Fetch tasks from the same job can run concurrently, although no particular assignment to
threads is guaranteed. All fetch tasks of a job share a countdown, and the fetch task that brings it to zero completes the job's I/O.

A worker thread claims the oldest job in the queue and checks that countdown. If I/O is done, the worker starts decoding the job. If not, it parks the scan task and is free to run other pipeline tasks. The last fetch task then unblocks the scan task, which may resume on any regular worker.
Claiming the job also immediately frees a queue slot, allowing any regular worker looking for scan work to produce a replacement job at the back of the queue. The figure below depicts this cycle:

content_blocks.alt: Read-ahead cycle
Read-ahead cycle

children.text: Keeping more fetch tasks in flight consumes more memory. To determine a budget and avoid out-of-memory issues, we introduced the
configuration option. It can have three types of values:
jobs ahead, with no memory budget.
: read-ahead is off, each scan task schedules I/O only for its own job.

content_blocks.text: SETread_ahead_depth=5;

children.text: In the default mode, the budget is negotiated with the temporary memory manager, which is the same manager that splits memory between concurrent joins, sorts, and window operators. When there is a lot of memory pressure, for example, because an operator is using a large amount of memory, queue reservations might instantly be over budget. In practice, this means that the queue will only allow one job at a time, and the scan will behave close to a synchronous scan.
When the memory-heavy operator finishes, the memory manager has more budget to give, and the queue fills back up.
Asynchronous I/O should have the largest effect when the latency of synchronous requests prevents us from using the available remote bandwidth. To measure this effect, we ran
, with the data sitting on S3, and compared the results against
, our latest stable release. The SF100 dataset was written as a single file per table for both the Parquet and CSV benchmarks, with the
For compute, we used an EC2

machine (64 vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM), with both the machine and the S3 bucket with the data located in the same region. We executed the query five times and report the mean execution time. The files were never cached (i.e.,
), meaning that every execution read the data straight from S3.

The Parquet file is approximately 22 GB and has around 4,880 row groups, with each row group containing approximately 122,880 rows. With asynchronous I/O, the mean runtime drops from 8.230 seconds to 2.844 seconds, making the query almost 3× faster.
Below we also show the network throughput over the course of the query:

content_blocks.alt: Network throughput
Network throughput

children.text: In it, we run DuckDB v1.5.5 and two variations of DuckDB v2.0.0-dev. One with the read-ahead depth determined by the memory governor, and one tuned for this machine, where we cap the read-ahead at 64 in-flight jobs and adjust the I/O settings (
SET async_threads = 48; SET http_retries = 8; SET http_retry_wait_ms = 50; SET http_retry_backoff = 2

). We can see that v2.0.0-dev uses the available bandwidth much more effectively, approaching the network limit and reaching it at several points. The tuned version goes further. With fewer, hotter connections and cheap retries, the throughput variance drops to a minimum and the 25 Gbit/s network stays almost fully saturated. Its query time was 2.227 seconds, reducing the runtime of the untuned v2.0.0-dev run by 21.7% and making it about 3.7× faster than DuckDB v1.5.5. In comparison, v1.5.5 stays around 5 Gbit/s because its synchronous reads do not keep enough requests in flight to saturate the network.

One other detail worth noting is that, in all experiments, a few hundred milliseconds pass before the first bump in network traffic, followed by another few hundred milliseconds before the main data transfer begins. The first gap is the time needed to open a DuckDB connection, perform the first TLS handshake, and open the file. The bump corresponds to downloading the file footer, while the second gap comes from processing the information in the footer before executing the query. We believe this is an area we can investigate and optimize further before the v2.0 release.

We sampled the NIC's received-byte counter every 50 ms and calculated the throughput from the change in bytes between samples. We independently confirmed that the machine can access the network at 25 Gbit/s with both a DuckDB full-file read and the

Remote storage is the main target for asynchronous I/O, but cold local reads give us a useful contrast. To measure them, we ran TPC-H Query 6 over the SF100 Parquet file, this time with the file sitting on the local disk of a MacBook Pro (Apple M4 Max, 14 cores, and 36 GB of RAM). Since the benefit of asynchronous I/O on local disks comes from cold reads, we cleared the OS caches (with the macOS
command) between runs, making sure every execution actually read the file from disk.

We can see that, for cold runs, asynchronous I/O is approximately 1.5× faster, reducing runtime by about 33%. The performance difference is much smaller than in the cases presented above, due to the SSD having much lower latency and much higher bandwidth than the EC2/S3 network. For hot runs, the difference is negligible, as there is no disk access happening if data is properly cached.

Partitioned datasets are a particularly relevant use case here, as partitioning can easily spread the data across many small files. To see how asynchronous I/O behaves in this setup, we also performed a Parquet run using the same TPC-H SF100 dataset. Instead of using one file, we generated 976 files with five row groups each. Each file contains approximately 615,000 rows and is around 22 MB in size.

We can see that v2.0.0-dev delivers a similar performance improvement here as it does for the single-file benchmark, running around 3× faster. This shows that read-ahead can also parallelize across multiple files without becoming bottlenecked by opening files or fetching their footers.
We also wanted to see what happens at the other extreme, when a Parquet file has only a few very large row groups. For this experiment, we generated six versions of the same TPC-H SF100
table as a single file, changing only the requested row group (RG) size, and ran Q6 using DuckDB v2.0.0-dev. The table below reports the runtime for each version.

At first, larger row groups decrease query times. As we increase the row-group size, request latency is amortized over much larger transfers. However, beyond a certain point, the available parallelism starts to fall. A row group is DuckDB's unit of Parquet scan parallelism, so ideally a scan should expose at least one row group per system thread. On this 64-vCPU machine, the version with 64 row groups provides exactly that and finishes in 2.27 seconds, while the fastest run comes from the version with 306 row groups, at 2.11 seconds.

However, with fewer row groups than threads, we lose parallelism and can no longer saturate the network. For Q6, the projections and the physical location of the columns result in two fetch requests per row group. Four row groups therefore expose only about eight concurrent S3 streams, raising the runtime to 8.01 seconds. For the largest configuration, the file contains a single row group, and its I/O is effectively reduced to two giant streams, pushing the runtime to 25.26 seconds. This happens even though better compression makes the file a little over half the size of the version with 4,886 row groups. In this case, the extra bandwidth required by smaller row groups is cheaper than the parallelism lost with extremely large ones.

The effect becomes even clearer when several queries run at the same time. We picked these queries because they cover a mix of scans, aggregations, and joins, with different CPU and memory requirements. We report the average and peak CPU utilization (number of cores utilized), the peak bandwidth (bw.) and the peak resident set size (RSS).

With the default memory configuration, DuckDB v1.5.5 keeps an average of only about 6 of the 64 cores busy. In other words, around 90% of the machine sits idle waiting for synchronous S3 reads. DuckDB v2.0.0-dev, on the other hand, averages 48 busy cores, reaches all 64 at its peak, and saturates the 25 Gbit/s network. As a result, all four queries finish in less than half the time.

The memory results are also interesting. As we lower the limit, the memory governor reduces the read-ahead backlog, while memory-heavy operators such as those in Q18 can spill to disk. This lowers the peak physical memory used by the DuckDB process (i.e., RSS) of DuckDB v2.0.0-dev from 20.1 GB with the default configuration to 15.7 GB with a 16 GB limit and 11.5 GB with an 8 GB limit. The additional spilling and reduced read-ahead also lower average CPU utilization and increase the runtime, but v2.0.0-dev continues to saturate the network and remains substantially faster than v1.5.5 in both cases.
One might notice that the 8 GB result still peaks at 11.5 GB of RSS. This is because
keeps recently freed pages resident for about one second so they can be reused. This memory is no longer counted by DuckDB's memory manager, and v1.5.5 shows the same allocator behavior.

The effect is larger on CSV files. The CSV file is 80.89 GB, and asynchronous I/O reduces the mean runtime from 878 seconds to just 45 seconds, making the query almost 20× faster. CSV is row-oriented, so the scan transfers substantially more data and performs fixed-size buffer reads, making concurrent remote reads especially valuable.
As in the other experiments, we used the default memory-governed read-ahead depth, so this run was not tuned to keep the 25 Gbit/s network saturated on average.

In this blog post, we presented the recent work on asynchronous I/O for Parquet and CSV files. Most of its benefit comes from accessing remote data, but cold local reads can also benefit, albeit less. Next, we plan to add async reads for JSON and DuckDB-native files, as these are the two other formats most relevant to DuckDB core. Formats that live in out-of-tree extensions are not on the roadmap yet. We will also investigate

, Linux's asynchronous I/O interface, which could reduce system-call overhead and the number of threads blocked on I/O. If it proves beneficial in practice, we will integrate it into DuckDB. events.reason: 对话式分析正在从独立聊天框进入Dashboard主工作流，权限继承和受治理语义将成为ChatBI落地的关键。
events.full_zh:
Tableau Agent in Dashboards (Beta)

Applies to: Tableau Cloud, Tableau Desktop

Tableau Agent in Dashboards is a pilot or beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at Agreements - Salesforce.com(Link opens in a new window) or a written Unified Pilot Agreement if executed by Customer, and the Non-GA Gen AI, Non-GA Open AI LLM Provider, and Non-GA Multiple Infrastructure terms in the Product Terms Directory(Link opens in a new window). Use of this pilot or beta service consumes Customer Data Cloud Credits as applicable and use is at the Customer's sole discretion.

As a data analyst, you work hard to put together dashboards for business users to help them find data insights fast to take action on the things that matter most. However, it can take time for these consumers to find the right insights, go through the dashboard to find the right data to focus on, or even know if this dashboard is meant for them.

In addition, they might have questions or want to dive deeper to understand certain data points. This can result in additional work for you, the author.

Meet Tableau Agent in Dashboards, an AI assistant for your dashboard consumers. Tableau Agent can provide an overview about the data in a dashboard and quickly get relevant insights with the simple click of a button. Users can also ask deep dive questions about the underlying data by simply typing their question into a text box using natural language.

Tableau Agent can't help you build a dashboard. But it can serve up a short summary about the dashboard, insights by chart, and answer questions with text and tables.

Tableau Dashabord with the Tableau Agent pane open and showing an overview, insights and answers to questions.

What's included

Tableau Agent in Dashboards includes 3 capabilities:

Dashboard Overview  Dashboard Insights  Dashboard Q&A

All of these features keep your security in mind by strictly adhering to all of your existing Tableau permissions, access controls, and row-level security. Users will only be able to access the data that you want them to see. To fully use all of these capabilities, users must be assigned the AI Access and Full Data Query permissions. For more information, see Prerequisites.

Dashboard Overview

Supported in Tableau Cloud and Tableau Desktop version 2026.1 and later

Dashboard Overview scans the visualizations in a dashboard and returns a summary to tell the viewer what the dashboard is about. This helps dashboard consumers get context about the dashboard, helps them on-board quickly and know that the dashboard is for them.

As a dashboard author, you can turn this capability on or off per dashboard.

Tableau dashboard with Tableau Agent open and showing a dashboard summary.

Dashboard Insights

Supported in Tableau Cloud and Tableau Desktop version 2026.1 and later

Dashboard Insights creates a set of summary insights based on the vizzes in the dashboard. It doesn't access or include any unused fields in your data source in the insights it creates. With Dashboard Insights, dashboard consumers can quickly focus on the insights that matter most, viz by viz.

As a dashboard author, you can control which visualizations and insights to include. You can also turn this capability on or off per dashboard.

Tableau dashboard with Tableau Agent open and showing insights per viz.

As an author, you can turn Dashboard Narratives on or off for consumers on a per-dashboard basis. You can also configure the dashboard narrative to include or exclude certain worksheets, or focus on only certain types of insights.

Tableau Agent can create the following types of insights:

Note: Dashboard Insights works best with published data sources. If your dashboard uses a local data source, then only Unexpected Values (outliers) are returned

Insight type Definition Concentrated ContributionShows when a small number of dimension members make up a majority (50% or more) of the contribution to a metric.Top DriversShows values for dimension members that changed the most in the same direction as the observed change in the metric.Current TrendShows current trends to communicate the rate of change, direction, and fluctuations for the metric value.Trend ChangeShows new trends that vary significantly from the current trend. This insight communicates the rate of change, direction, and fluctuations for the metric value.Bottom ContributorsShows the lowest values in a dimension for a metric within a given time range.Top DetractorsShows values for dimension members that changed the most in the opposite direction to the observed change in the metric.Unexpected Values (outliers)Shows when the value of a metric for a given time range is higher or lower than the expected range based on historic observations of the metric.

Dashboard Q&A

Supported in Tableau Cloud (with Tableau Cloud+ or Tableau+) version 2026.2.4 and later

When you have a question about your dashboard or just want to dive deeper into the data, Dashboard Q&A is the answer. With the appropriate permissions, even Viewers can type in a question about their data and Tableau Agent will query the underlying data source.

With Dashboard Q&A, you can ask "What" and "Why" questions using natural language. For example "What California facilities classified as urgent care have an average wait time of > 90 minutes?". "Why does "Customer A" have a large negative profit?".

Tableau Agent can answer these questions using the workbook's data source, whether published or embedded.

Tableau Agent can respond with text and tables, and you can dig deeper into a response to see how it came up with the answer. Dashboard Q&A shows all of the reasoning steps that Tableau Agent took to find its answer, as well as a summary of the data it used, so you can be confident that the response is accurate.

As a dashboard author, you can turn this capability on or off per dashboard.

Tableau dashboard showing a response from Tableau Agent.

Tableau Agent and Trust

Tableau Agent is built on top of the Einstein Trust Layer(Link opens in a new window) and inherits all of its security, governance, and Trust capabilities. As you interact with Tableau Agent, any data that is sent to the Large Language Model (LLM) isn't saved to the LLM, and no customer data is ever used to train the model.

The Einstein Trust Layer can be used to mask Personally Identifying Information (PII) before it is sent to the LLM using pattern-based data masking. Using machine learning and pattern matching techniques, PII in prompts are replaced with generic tokens and then unmasked with original values in the response. For more information about how to configure data masking, see Select What Data to Mask(Link opens in a new window) in the Salesforce help. For an additional layer of protection, the Einstein Trust Layer guarantees that after the prompt and response are processed by the LLM, the LLM forgets both the prompt and the response.

Prerequisites

Before you can use Tableau Agent in Tableau Dashboards complete the following prerequisites:

Connect to a Tableau Cloud+, Tableau+ Cloud site, or Tableau Cloud trial site.  (Admin) Ensure the AI in Tableau site setting for Tableau Agent for Dashboard Consumers is turned on. For more information, see Turn On AI in Your Tableau Cloud Site(Link opens in a new window).  (Admin, project leader, or content owner) Grant the workbook permissions AI Access and Full Data Query for your dashboard users. For more information see Permissions(Link opens in a new window).  (Author) Use the Tableau Agent Best Practices checklist(Link opens in a new window) to make sure your data source, workbooks, and dashboard are optimized for Tableau Agent.

Who can do this

Your site role will affect what you can do with Tableau Agent in dashboards.

Creator and Site Administrator Creator: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in authoring and viewing mode. Configure settings in authoring mode.Explorer (can publish) and Site Administrator Explorer: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in authoring and viewing mode. Configure settings in authoring mode.Explorer: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in viewing mode.Viewer: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in viewing mode. AI Access and The Full Data Query workbook permission are required.

Tableau Agent can't help you build a dashboard. But it can serve up a short summary about the dashboard, insights by chart, and answer questions with text and tables.

content_blocks.alt: Tableau Dashabord with the Tableau Agent pane open and showing an overview, insights and answers to questions.

children.text: Tableau Agent in Dashboards includes 3 capabilities:

All of these features keep your security in mind by strictly adhering to all of your existing Tableau permissions, access controls, and row-level security. Users will only be able to access the data that you want them to see. To fully use all of these capabilities, users must be assigned the AI Access and Full Data Query permissions. For more information, see
Supported in Tableau Cloud and Tableau Desktop version 2026.1 and later

Dashboard Overview scans the visualizations in a dashboard and returns a summary to tell the viewer what the dashboard is about. This helps dashboard consumers get context about the dashboard, helps them on-board quickly and know that the dashboard is for them.
As a dashboard author, you can turn this capability on or off per dashboard.

content_blocks.alt: Tableau dashboard with Tableau Agent open and showing a dashboard summary.

children.text: Supported in Tableau Cloud and Tableau Desktop version 2026.1 and later

Dashboard Insights creates a set of summary insights based on the vizzes in the dashboard. It doesn't access or include any unused fields in your data source in the insights it creates. With Dashboard Insights, dashboard consumers can quickly focus on the insights that matter most, viz by viz.
As a dashboard author, you can control which visualizations and insights to include. You can also turn this capability on or off per dashboard.

content_blocks.alt: Tableau dashboard with Tableau Agent open and showing insights per viz.

children.text: As an author, you can turn Dashboard Narratives on or off for consumers on a per-dashboard basis. You can also configure the dashboard narrative to include or exclude certain worksheets, or focus on only certain types of insights.
Tableau Agent can create the following types of insights:
: Dashboard Insights works best with published data sources. If your dashboard uses a local data source, then only Unexpected Values (outliers) are returned
Shows when a small number of dimension members make up a majority (50% or more) of the contribution to a metric.
Shows values for dimension members that changed the most in the same direction as the observed change in the metric.
Shows current trends to communicate the rate of change, direction, and fluctuations for the metric value.
Shows new trends that vary significantly from the current trend. This insight communicates the rate of change, direction, and fluctuations for the metric value.
Shows the lowest values in a dimension for a metric within a given time range.
Shows values for dimension members that changed the most in the opposite direction to the observed change in the metric.
Shows when the value of a metric for a given time range is higher or lower than the expected range based on historic observations of the metric.
Supported in Tableau Cloud (with Tableau Cloud+ or Tableau+) version 2026.2.4 and later

When you have a question about your dashboard or just want to dive deeper into the data, Dashboard Q&A is the answer. With the appropriate permissions, even Viewers can type in a question about their data and Tableau Agent will query the underlying data source.

With Dashboard Q&A, you can ask "What" and "Why" questions using natural language. For example "What California facilities classified as urgent care have an average wait time of > 90 minutes?". "Why does "Customer A" have a large negative profit?".
Tableau Agent can answer these questions using the workbook's data source, whether published or embedded.

Tableau Agent can respond with text and tables, and you can dig deeper into a response to see how it came up with the answer. Dashboard Q&A shows all of the reasoning steps that Tableau Agent took to find its answer, as well as a summary of the data it used, so you can be confident that the response is accurate.
As a dashboard author, you can turn this capability on or off per dashboard.

content_blocks.alt: Tableau dashboard showing a response from Tableau Agent.

children.text: Tableau Agent is built on top of the
Einstein Trust Layer(Link opens in a new window)

and inherits all of its security, governance, and Trust capabilities. As you interact with Tableau Agent, any data that is sent to the Large Language Model (LLM) isn't saved to the LLM, and no customer data is ever used to train the model.

The Einstein Trust Layer can be used to mask Personally Identifying Information (PII) before it is sent to the LLM using pattern-based data masking. Using machine learning and pattern matching techniques, PII in prompts are replaced with generic tokens and then unmasked with original values in the response. For more information about how to configure data masking, see
Select What Data to Mask(Link opens in a new window)

in the Salesforce help. For an additional layer of protection, the Einstein Trust Layer guarantees that after the prompt and response are processed by the LLM, the LLM forgets both the prompt and the response.
Before you can use Tableau Agent in Tableau Dashboards complete the following prerequisites:
Connect to a Tableau Cloud+, Tableau+ Cloud site, or Tableau Cloud trial site.
(Admin) Ensure the AI in Tableau site setting for Tableau Agent for Dashboard Consumers is turned on. For more information, see
Turn On AI in Your Tableau Cloud Site(Link opens in a new window)
(Admin, project leader, or content owner) Grant the workbook permissions AI Access and Full Data Query for your dashboard users. For more information see
Permissions(Link opens in a new window)
Best Practices checklist(Link opens in a new window)
to make sure your data source, workbooks, and dashboard are optimized for Tableau Agent.
Your site role will affect what you can do with Tableau Agent in dashboards.
: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in authoring and viewing mode. Configure settings in authoring mode.
: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in authoring and viewing mode. Configure settings in authoring mode.
: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in viewing mode.
: See and use Tableau Agent in Dashboards in viewing mode. AI Access and The Full Data Query workbook permission are required.

events.zh_title: 跨100+ AWS账户的集中CloudTrail监控
events.zh_summary: AWS Big Data Blog 介绍了如何在 Amazon OpenSearch Service 上构建集中式 CloudTrail 监控方案，使用 Terraform 管理全栈资源。该方案每日处理 200 GB 日志，覆盖 100+ AWS 账户，提供自动化威胁检测，并支持按需生成 SOC 2、PCI DSS 和 HIPAA 合规报告，同时为四个团队提供隔离的权限访问。
events.reason: 面向大规模多云账户的安全日志集中分析与合规报告实践，对数据平台建设者具有参考价值。

children.text: 跨100多个AWS账户的集中式CloudTrail监控
在数十或数百个AWS账户中运行工作负载的组织面临一个常见挑战：大规模集中式安全监控。安全团队需要每天搜索数百GB的AWS CloudTrail日志，以检测威胁并满足SOC 2、PCI DSS和HIPAA审计的合规要求。他们还需要为职责不同的多个团队提供基于角色的访问。
如果没有专用基础设施，这通常涉及耗时数小时的手动日志搜索和耗时数天的合规报告生成。它还导致跨环境管理索引生命周期的自定义AWS Lambda函数代码库碎片化。一个没有一致访问控制的共享搜索域进一步加剧了问题。
在本文中，我们展示了如何在Amazon OpenSearch Service上构建集中式CloudTrail监控解决方案。Terraform管理整个堆栈，从域配置到访问控制和生命周期策略。该解决方案处理每天200GB的CloudTrail日志，提供自动威胁检测警报，并为4个不同团队提供隔离的、适合角色的数据访问。

下图显示了架构。CloudTrail日志通过组织跟踪从100多个AWS账户流入集中式S3存储桶。Amazon Simple Queue Service（Amazon SQS）通知触发OpenSearch Ingestion管道。该管道在2到10个OpenSearch计算单元（OCU）之间自动扩展，以将日志解析并索引到OpenSearch域中。四个团队特定角色通过OpenSearch Dashboards访问数据，并实现租户隔离。

content_blocks.alt: CloudTrail日志从100多个账户流入S3，然后通过Amazon SQS和OpenSearch Ingestion进入被4个团队角色使用的OpenSearch域

children.text: 组织跟踪将100多个账户的日志发送到集中式Amazon Simple Storage Service（Amazon S3）存储桶。
Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion管道通过S3存储桶上的Amazon SQS通知拾取新日志。它根据队列深度在2到10个OCU之间自动扩展。较低环境队列上的限制可防止开发和测试峰值饿死生产摄取。
6个或1.4xlarge数据节点（OpenSearch优化实例）和3个专用r8g.large主节点，具有细粒度访问控制、静态加密和节点间加密。
索引模板、索引状态管理（ISM）策略、角色、角色映射、租户、警报监控器和仪表板全部在Terraform中声明，并在环境中一致应用。
要实现此解决方案，您需要以下各项：
在AWS Organizations中启用CloudTrail并在成员账户中启用的组织。
具有用于OpenSearch域的私有子网的虚拟私有云（VPC）。
每个将访问OpenSearch域的团队的IAM角色。
用于安全警报通知的Amazon Simple Notification Service（Amazon SNS）主题。
本节逐步介绍解决方案每个组件的Terraform代码，从指导我们大小调整决策的工作负载配置文件开始。
在调整集群大小之前，我们定义了集中式CloudTrail监控平台的工作负载特征和SLA：
这是一个写重的摄取工作负载。主要用例是自动警报和定期合规查询，而不是连续交互式搜索。此工作负载配置文件指导了使用OR1（存储优化）实例和零副本的决策，优先考虑索引吞吐量而非搜索并行性。
首先配置Amazon OpenSearch Service域，启用加密、细粒度访问控制和VPC放置：

Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion管道提供从Amazon S3到OpenSearch域的无服务器自动扩展摄取。它通过集中式S3存储桶上的Amazon SQS通知拾取新的CloudTrail日志，并根据队列深度在2到10个OpenSearch计算单元（OCU）之间扩展：
该管道使用带有基于SQS通知的S3源插件。当新的CloudTrail日志文件到达S3时，SQS消息触发管道获取并解析它们。
参数控制自动扩展。管道从2个OCU开始，根据队列深度扩展到10个，无需手动干预即可处理摄取峰值。对于较低环境（开发和测试），您可以对Amazon SQS队列应用限制，以防止非生产峰值饿死生产摄取容量。
提前定义索引模板，避免日后痛苦的重新索引。以下模板为 CloudTrail 字段设置显式映射，通过异步 translog 持久性优化写入吞吐量，并与 ISM 集成实现自动滚动：
在数据摄入前定义映射可防止映射冲突，并避免事后重新索引数据。
生命周期管理（ISM 策略）

对于每天摄入超过 100 GB 的索引（例如本部署中的 CloudTrail 每天 200 GB），您可以将

当多个团队需要对同一数据具有不同访问级别时，请声明式地定义所有角色，并使用
一致地创建它们。以下示例定义了 4 个具有不同权限的团队角色：
此方法将 IAM 角色（而非单个用户）映射到 OpenSearch 角色。添加新团队只需在

。每个团队在 OpenSearch Dashboards 中获得隔离的租户，防止跨团队干扰已保存的搜索、可视化和仪表板配置。我们选择 OpenSearch Dashboards 是因为租户、角色、可视化和已保存对象都可以通过 Terraform OpenSearch provider 以编程方式管理，使整个堆栈处于基础设施即代码治理之下。对于在 Terraform 管理工作流之外构建新可视化的团队，我们推荐

在 Terraform 中定义告警监控器以自动检测安全关键事件。以下监控器捕获 CloudTrail 篡改尝试（StopLogging、DeleteTrail）并通过 Amazon SNS 发送告警：
部署解决方案后，我们根据工作负载配置文件中定义的 SLA 测量了稳态性能：
通过已保存搜索按需生成
威胁检测从数小时缩短到数分钟。
自动化告警取代了手动日志搜索。CloudTrail 篡改监控器在事件发生后一分钟内检测到可疑活动。
借助 600 多个已保存搜索和 100 多个仪表板，合规团队在几分钟内即可生成 SOC 2、PCI DSS 和 HIPAA 审计证据，而不是几天。
每个团队在 OpenSearch Dashboards 中拥有自己的隔离租户，防止跨团队干扰已保存搜索和仪表板配置。
零自定义 Lambda 函数。
ISM 策略、索引模板和访问控制全部通过 Terraform 声明式管理，消除了之前分散的代码库。
在摄入任何数据之前定义索引模板。更改现有索引的映射意味着重新索引。首先正确完成这一步。
根据实际摄入速率设置滚动阈值。在每天 200 GB 的情况下，在 30 GB 处滚动保持分片数量可控，同时平衡查询性能。
先在低环境测试 ISM 转换。大型索引的热到温冷迁移需要时间。
映射 IAM 角色而不是用户。人员会变更团队。角色保持稳定。这简化了访问管理。
在 S3 和摄取管道之间放置一个 Amazon SQS 队列。这为您提供每个环境的节流控制，而无需修改管道配置。
。角色、租户、索引模式和监控器都跨团队或环境遵循模式，因此使用
考虑为新的可视化工作流使用 OpenSearch UI。该解决方案使用 OpenSearch Dashboards 管理 Terraform 管理的租户和角色。OpenSearch UI 是一个下一代界面，支持多数据源，在集群升级期间保持可用，并包含用于团队隔离的工作区。它是创建新仪表板和可视化的推荐界面。
可选：通过冷存储扩展以实现更长的保留期
对于有合规要求强制更长保留期的组织（例如，PCI DSS 或 HIPAA 要求 7 年），您可以使用温冷层扩展 ISM 策略。以下示例添加了分层存储，将数据按热、温、冷和删除状态移动：
温存储使用 force-merge 减少段数量（降低查询开销），而冷存储将数据完全移动到 Amazon S3 以最小化成本。这种分层方法保持热层的高性能，同时满足长期审计要求。

events.reason: 数据从业者可在BigQuery内直接调用最新Gemini模型进行生成式分析，降低AI功能集成成本。
events.full_zh:
Home     Documentation     Data analytics     BigQuery     Resources

BigQuery release notes   Stay organized with collections   Save and categorize content based on your preferences.

This page documents production updates to BigQuery. We recommend that BigQuery developers periodically check this list for any new announcements. BigQuery automatically updates to the latest release and cannot be downgraded to a previous version.

For older release notes, see the Release notes archive.

You can see the latest product updates for all of Google Cloud on the  Google Cloud page, browse and filter all release notes in the Google Cloud console, or programmatically access release notes in BigQuery.

To get the latest product updates delivered to you, add the URL of this page to your feed reader, or add the feed URL directly.

August 11, 2026

Feature Query templates for data clean rooms are generally available (GA). Query templates allow data clean room owners and publishers to share predefined queries without exposing the underlying tables and views.

Additionally, table parameters in table-valued functions (TVFs) are generally available (GA). You can use the ANY TABLE type as a table parameter to create generic functions that accept tables of any structure.

August 10, 2026

Feature BigQuery now supports the gemini-3.1-flash-lite and gemini-3.5-flash GA models, which are available for the us, eu, and global multi-regional endpoints. You can use these models in all generative AI functions. For information about how to specify a multi-regional endpoint and how endpoints are selected, read about locations in the generative AI overview.

August 03, 2026

Feature You can now use cross-cloud connections to query data in AWS, Azure, and Salesforce Data 360 from all BigQuery regions. These connections let you use more BigQuery features and are more cost efficient than standard connections that use BigQuery Omni. This feature is in Preview.

Feature The JDBC driver for BigQuery now supports OpenTelemetry for tracing and logging, which helps you monitor the performance of your database interactions and troubleshoot issues. Automatic exports to Google Cloud Observability are also available. This feature is generally available (GA).

Announcement Support for hybrid search (using the VECTOR_SEARCH function to combine a semantic search with a lexical (keyword) search) has been restored. Using HYBRID mode in the AI.SEARCH function has also been restored.

July 30, 2026

Feature You can add tables, views, data sources, and data quality tests as tasks to BigQuery pipelines. For more information, see Add a pipeline task. This feature is generally available.

Feature You can audit when users download query results by using the BigQuery console. Data Access audit logs for the tabledata.list method now include a uiDownloadRequest field to indicate whether the request was triggered by a UI download. This feature is generally available (GA).

July 29, 2026

Feature The BigQuery Data Transfer Service now supports incremental data transfers when transferring data from Klaviyo to BigQuery. This feature is supported in Preview.

July 27, 2026

Feature You can discover commercial BigQuery sharing listings on Google Cloud Marketplace with the Marketplace filter. For more information, see Subscribe to a Cloud Marketplace-integrated listing. This feature is generally available (GA).

Feature You can use the APPENDS and CHANGES change history functions to view the rows that were appended to or changed in a table during a given time range. This feature is generally available (GA).

Feature You can use the Google-developed Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) driver for BigQuery to connect your applications to BigQuery. This feature is generally available (GA).

Change The feature formerly known as the legacy tabledata.insertAll method is now called the Storage Write API (REST). The feature formerly known as the Storage Write API is now called the Storage Write API (gRPC).

Feature BigQuery dataset insights is generally available (GA).

BigQuery dataset insights helps you discover and visualize relationships between tables and automatically generate cross-table queries. You can run and publish these insights to Knowledge Catalog for agentic grounding use cases, or generate them on demand without publishing for quick, ad hoc dataset exploration.

July 23, 2026

Change An updated version of the Simba ODBC driver for BigQuery is now available.

July 20, 2026

Issue Lakehouse for Apache Iceberg: Data Products with special characters, such as "/" or "-", are not supported and will not be available in BigQuery even if shared from SAP BDC to BigQuery. If you share a Data Product with special characters, this could cause the refresh to stop and require re-enrollment. Known SAP systems producing these Data Products include SAP Business Warehouse (BW) sources and SAP SuccessFactors.

Feature Lakehouse for Apache Iceberg: Cross-cloud Lakehouse now supports integration with SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) in Preview.

This update includes the following features:

Federation from SAP BDC: Create Delta Sharing catalogs in Lakehouse to automatically synchronize shares, schemas, and tables from SAP BDC.Querying SAP data: Query synchronized SAP BDC tables directly from BigQuery without data migration.Publishing to SAP BDC: Publish Apache Iceberg REST catalog (IRC) tables or Knowledge Catalog Data Products from Lakehouse directly to SAP BDC, allowing SAP users and applications to consume Google Cloud data directly as remote tables in SAP Datasphere without migrating data.

For more information, see Set up cross-cloud Lakehouse for SAP BDC, Query SAP BDC data, and Publish Data Products to SAP BDC.

July 15, 2026

Feature BigQuery supports data governance tags, which let you enforce column-level security and data masking. Data governance tags are a type of Resource Manager tag that you can attach to sensitive columns and use in BigQuery data policies to grant conditional access to your users. This feature is in Preview.

July 14, 2026

Feature Conversational analytics now supports the AI.AGG function. This function is in Preview.

Announcement As part of Gemini in BigQuery, conversational analytics now supports HIPAA compliance.

July 13, 2026

Feature Table partitioning, multi-statement transactions, and advanced runtime are now generally available (GA) for Apache Iceberg managed tables.

Feature Cross-cloud Lakehouse now supports Snowflake as a remote catalog provider (Preview). You can configure federated catalogs to query data stored in Snowflake directly from Google Cloud using BigQuery or Apache Spark without migrating data or building complex ETL pipelines.

For more information, see Set up cross-cloud Lakehouse for Snowflake.

Security A Missing Authorization vulnerability was discovered in repositories in BigQuery, Dataform, and Colab Enterprise. An authenticated attacker could potentially escalate permissions and perform cross-tenant repository takeover. For more information, see the GCP-2026-047 security bulletin.

Feature Project caps (also known as scheduling policies) let you limit maximum slots and concurrency per project within a BigQuery reservation. This feature is in Preview.

Feature The BigQuery Overview page is a hub for discovering tutorials, features, and resources to help you get the most out of BigQuery. It provides guided paths for users of all skill levels. This feature is now generally available (GA).

Feature You can use the BigQuery Migration Service MCP server to perform SQL translation tasks, including translating SQL queries into GoogleSQL syntax, generating DDL statements from SQL input queries, and getting explanations of SQL translations.

This feature is Generally Available.

Feature Incremental data transfers for the BigQuery Data Transfer Service for Salesforce are now generally available (GA).

Feature You can now use the ALTER SEARCH INDEX DDL statement to update the configuration of a search index. This feature is in Preview.

July 09, 2026

Feature You can use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to transfer metadata from the following data sources into Knowledge Catalog:

Feature BigQuery now supports a RANDOM_HASH predefined masking rule. This rule returns a hash of the column's value using a salted hash algorithm, and it provides stronger security than the standard Hash (SHA-256) rule.

For more information, see Data masking rules.

Feature BigQuery now offers conversational analytics, which accelerates data analysis by enabling insights through natural language. Users can view a predefined sample agent, chat with their BigQuery data or custom agents, and access those agents even outside of BigQuery. They can also use supported BigQuery ML functions in verified queries and in chat. This feature is in Preview.

Feature You can now create BigQuery ML models by using the Google Cloud console.

This feature is generally available (GA).

January 28, 2026

Change The BigQuery change data capture feature has been renamed to BigQuery change data capture ingestion.

Feature The BigQuery Data Transfer Service can now transfer data from Shopify to BigQuery. This feature is in Preview.

January 27, 2026

Change An updated version of the Simba JDBC driver for BigQuery is now available.

Feature The BigQuery Data Transfer Service can now transfer data from Mailchimp to BigQuery. This feature is in Preview.

January 26, 2026

Feature You can now use Gemini Cloud Assist to discover resources across your projects. For example, you can ask about a specific table's schema, or which tables contain demographic information about new users. This feature is in Preview.

January 23, 2026

Change You can now optionally specify which model to use by passing an endpoint argument to the AI.IF, AI.SCORE, and AI.CLASSIFY functions.

January 22, 2026

Fixed Support for table parameters in table-valued functions is restored.

Change You can now run queries that use the AI.IF, AI.SCORE, and AI.CLASSIFY functions by using your end-user credentials instead of a BigQuery connection.

January 21, 2026

Change BigQuery is now available in the Bangkok (asia-southeast3) region.

Feature You can now use Gemini Cloud Assist to get information about your job history, such as why a particular query was slow or which queries were the most resource-intensive in the past day. This feature is in Preview.

January 19, 2026

Breaking Dataform workflows, BigQuery notebooks, pipelines, and data preparations are enforcing strict act-as mode at the project level. To avoid failures and maintain automatic releases, you must use custom service accounts instead of the default Dataform service agent across all repositories. You must also grant the Service Account User role (roles/iam.serviceAccountUser) to the default Dataform service agent and relevant principals. For more information and to verify act-as permissions, see Use strict act-as mode.

January 07, 2026

Feature You can now use the Google-developed, open source Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) driver for BigQuery to connect your Java applications to BigQuery. This feature is in Preview.

January 06, 2026

Feature The CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE and LOAD DATA statements now support the following options:

time_zone: specify a time zone to use when loading datadate_format, datetime_format, time_format, and timestamp_format: define how date and time values are formatted in your source filesnull_markers: define the strings that represent NULL values in CSV files.source_column_match: specify how loaded columns are matched to the schema. You can match columns by position or by name.

These features are generally available (GA).

December 22, 2025

Feature The BigQuery Data Transfer Service can now transfer data from PostgreSQL to BigQuery. This feature is generally available (GA).

Announcement BigQuery now provides spend-based committed use discounts (CUDs). Change You can get the required permissions to use BigQuery data preparation through the BigQuery Studio User (roles/bigquery.studioUser) and Gemini for Google Cloud User (roles/cloudaicompanion.user) roles, and permission to access the data you're preparing.

April 17, 2025

Feature You can use partial ordering mode in BigQuery DataFrames to generate efficient queries. This feature is generally available (GA).

Feature You can now use BigQuery DataFrames version 2.0, which makes security and performance improvements to the BigQuery DataFrames API, adds new features, and introduces breaking changes.

April 09, 2025

Announcement Dataplex Catalog has been renamed BigQuery universal catalog. You'll see this new name in the product page of the Google Cloud console, the documentation set, and the marketing collateral. Universal catalog brings together the data catalog capabilities of Dataplex Catalog and the runtime metastore capabilities of BigQuery metastore. For more information, see Introduction to data governance in BigQuery.

Change Updated pricing, packaging, and setup guidance is now available for Gemini in BigQuery.

Feature You can now use the Apache Arrow format to stream data to BigQuery with the Storage Write API. This feature is available in preview.

Change Analytics Hub has been renamed BigQuery sharing. You'll see this new name in the documentation set and the marketing collateral. The product functionality and endpoints remain the same. For more information, see Introduction to data governance in BigQuery.

Feature You can now combine raster and vector data with the ST_REGIONSTATS geography function to perform geospatial analysis in BigQuery. For more information, see Work with raster data and try the tutorial that shows you how to use raster data to analyze global temperature by country. This feature is in preview.

April 08, 2025

Feature You can now create, view, modify, and delete Apache Iceberg resources in BigQuery metastore. This feature is generally available (GA).

Feature You can now connect BigQuery metastore to Apache Flink. This feature is generally available (GA).

Feature BigQuery ML now offers a built-in TimesFM univariate time series forecasting model that implements Google Research's open source TimesFM model. You can use BigQuery ML's built-in TimesFM model with the AI.FORECAST function to perform forecasting without having to create and train your own model. This lets you avoid the need for model management.

To try using a TimesFM model with the AI.FORECAST function, see Forecast a time series with a TimesFM univariate model.

This feature is in preview.

April 07, 2025

Feature You can now create remote models in BigQuery ML based on Llama and Mistral AI models in Vertex AI.

Use the ML.GENERATE_TEXT function with these remote models to perform generative natural language tasks for text stored in BigQuery tables. Try this feature with the Generate text by using the ML.GENERATE_TEXT function tutorial.

This feature is generally available (GA).

Change An updated version of JDBC driver for BigQuery is now available.

Feature BigQuery data preparation is generally available (GA). It offers AI-powered suggestions from Gemini for data cleansing, transformation, and enrichment. BigQuery supports visual data preparation pipelines and pipeline scheduling with Dataform.

Feature Smart-tuning is now supported for materialized views when they are in the same project as one of their base tables, or when they are in the project running the query. This feature is generally available (GA).

Change BigQuery ML now uses dynamic token-based batching for embedding generation requests. Dynamic token-based batching puts as many rows as possible into one request. This change boosts per-request utilization and improves scalability for any queries per minute (QPM) quota. Actual performance varies based on the embedding content length, with an average 10x improvement.

April 04, 2025

Feature BigQuery ML now supports the following generative AI functions, which let you analyze text using a Vertex AI Gemini model. The function output includes a response that matches the type in the function name:

AI.GENERATEAI.GENERATE_BOOLAI.GENERATE_INTAI.GENERATE_DOUBLE

This feature is in preview.

April 03, 2025

Feature BigQuery migration assessment now includes support for Amazon Redshift Serverless. This feature is in  preview.

Feature You can now generate structured data by using BigQuery ML's AI.GENERATE_TABLE function with Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 1.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.0 Flash models. You can use the AI.GENERATE_TABLE function's output_schema argument to more easily format the model's response. The output_schema argument lets you specify a SQL schema for formatting, similar to the schema used in the CREATE TABLE statement. By creating structured output, you can more easily convert the function output into a BigQuery table.

Try this feature with the Generate structured data by using the AI.GENERATE_TABLE function tutorial.

This feature is in preview.

April 02, 2025

Feature You can now create and use Python user-defined functions (UDFs) in BigQuery. Python UDFs support the use of additional libraries and external APIs. This feature is in preview.

Change The Python code that you generate using Gemini in BigQuery Notebooks is now much more likely to leverage your data. With this change, BigQuery Notebooks can intelligently pull relevant table names directly from your BigQuery project, resulting in personalized, executable Python code.

Feature You can now generate Dataframes code in BigQuery Notebooks that use BigFrames libraries. In your code generation prompt, include the word BigFrames to generate code that uses BigQuery DataFrames. This feature is in preview.

April 01, 2025

Feature You can use a CREATE MODEL statement to create a contribution analysis model in BigQuery ML. The top_k_insights_by_apriori_support and pruning_method model options are now supported. You can use a contribution analysis model with the ML.GET_INSIGHTS function to generate insights about changes to key metrics in your multi-dimensional data. The following metric types are supported:

Summable metricSummable ratio metricSummable by category metric

This feature is generally available (GA).

Feature Pipe syntax supports a linear query structure designed to make your queries easier to read, write, and maintain. This feature is generally available (GA).

March 31, 2025

Feature Iceberg external tables now support merge-on-read. You can query Iceberg tables with position deletes and equality deletes. This feature is generally available (GA).

events.zh_title: Claude推出Cowork插件功能
events.zh_summary: Anthropic宣布为Cowork添加插件支持，允许用户将技能、连接器、斜杠命令和子代理捆绑在一起，使Claude成为针对特定角色、团队和公司的专家。插件可用于销售、法律和财务分析等场景，并开源了11个自有团队使用的插件。
events.reason: 这是Claude Code/Cowork产品更新，但核心是AI助理插件生态，与数据领域五大方向无直接关联。
events.full_zh:
使用插件定制Cowork

我们打造Cowork，旨在将Claude Code的强大功能带给所有人。今天，我们新增了对插件的支持，让您可以将任何技能、连接器、斜杠命令和子代理捆绑在一起，将Claude转变为适合您角色、团队和公司的专家。

类别产品公告代理产品Claude Enterprise日期：2026年1月30日阅读时间：5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/cowork-plugins

使用Cowork，您设定目标，Claude交付完成且专业的成果。插件让您更进一步：告诉Claude您喜欢的工作方式、要使用哪些工具和数据、如何处理关键工作流程，以及公开哪些斜杠命令，让您的团队获得更好、更一致的结果。

将插件与Cowork一起使用

插件适用于任何用例，但在针对销售、法律和财务分析等特定职能定制Claude时尤其强大。

例如，销售插件可以将Claude连接到您的CRM和知识库，教它您的销售流程，并为您提供从潜在客户研究到电话跟进的各种命令。您只需定义一次插件内容，Claude便会在相关时从该上下文中提取信息。

随着您的团队构建和共享插件，Claude成为跨职能专家。您分享的丰富上下文会被融入到每个相关交互中，因此领导和管理员可以花更少的时间执行流程，而花更多的时间改进流程。

插件市场

为了让您入门，我们开源了11个由我们团队构建和使用的插件：

生产力 — 管理任务、日历、日常工作流程和个人上下文企业搜索 — 在公司的工具和文档中查找信息插件创建/定制 — 从零开始创建和定制新插件销售 — 研究潜在客户、准备交易、遵循销售流程财务 — 分析财务数据、构建模型、跟踪关键指标数据 — 查询、可视化和解释数据集法律 — 审查文档、标记风险和跟踪合规性营销 — 起草内容、规划活动和管控发布客户支持 — 分类问题、起草回复和提供解决方案产品管理 — 编写规格、优先排序路线图和跟踪进度生物学研究 — 搜索文献、分析结果和规划实验

直接从Cowork安装这些插件，浏览我们网站上的完整集合，网站，或上传您自己的插件（可使用插件创建来构建）。它们也可供开发者在GitHub上获取。插件的每个组件（技能、连接器、斜杠命令和子代理）都基于文件，因此插件易于构建、编辑和共享。尝试使用Claude定制每个插件，使其适合您和您的团队。GitHub 供开发人员使用。插件的每个组件（技能、连接器、斜杠命令和子代理）都基于文件，因此易于构建、编辑和共享。尝试用Claude定制每个插件，使其完美适合您和您的团队。

开始使用

Cowork中的插件支持今天作为研究预览版向所有付费Claude用户开放。从我们的开源集合开始，对其进行定制，或构建全新的内容。

events.zh_title: Claude企业版Cowork与插件更新：私有市场与跨应用编排
events.zh_summary: Anthropic发布Claude企业版Cowork与插件更新，支持管理员创建私有插件市场，可控制插件、连接器和技能。新增多部门适用的插件和连接器，并支持Claude跨Excel和PowerPoint端到端编排。插件构建更简单，并新增统一'Customize'菜单管理插件、技能和连接器。
events.reason: 该更新涉及AI Agent在企业中的定制化分发与跨应用编排，对数据Agent和AI数据平台从业者了解企业级部署与管理实践有参考价值。
events.full_zh:
企业团队的 Cowork 与插件

管理员现在可以创建私有插件市场，更好地控制插件、连接器和技能。我们还在更多部门增加了新的插件和连接器。

类别代理企业 AI产品Claude Enterprise日期：2026年2月24日阅读时间：5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/cowork-plugins-across-enterprise

今天，我们宣布推出 Cowork 和插件的更新 帮助企业将 Claude 定制为符合您工作方式。插件将 Claude 转变为每个角色和部门的专业代理。现在，您可以构建私有市场，在整个组织中分发它们。

本次发布还使插件更易于构建和定制，赋予管理员对市场和连接器更多的控制权，并在更广泛的职位中增加新的插件和连接器。Claude 现在还可以跨 Excel 和 PowerPoint 进行编排，端到端地工作并在应用之间传递上下文。

‍

Silvern Capital 是一家虚构公司。演示中的大多数团队在 Cowork 中工作，而法务团队则在汤森路透 CoCounsel Legal 中工作——这是一个使用 Claude Agent SDK 从头构建的专门法律代理。

升级插件体验

今天，我们推出了一系列更新，使在整个组织中创建、使用和管理插件更加容易。

管理员现在可以从 Starter 模板设置插件或从头构建，Claude 会通过提问来引导您完成设置，以定制技能、命令和连接器（MCP）以适应您的公司。所有这些都集中在一个新的统一菜单“自定义”中，该菜单整合了插件、技能和连接器，使管理员可以在一个地方查看和管理所有内容。

连接器体验也经过了彻底改造，改进了目录、简化了管理控制，并更易于管理哪些连接器捆绑在插件中。管理员还对团队可以访问的插件拥有更多控制权，包括特定于组织的市场、作为插件源的私有 GitHub 仓库（私有测试版）、按用户配置和自动安装。

在用户方面，斜杠命令现在以结构化表单启动，因此运行诸如“生成报告”或“仪表板”之类的工作流程感觉像填写简报一样直观。Cowork 现在在整个过程中都包含公司品牌，包括为您的组织量身定制的重新设计的首页体验。

此外，我们正在添加OpenTelemetry支持，让管理员能够跟踪其团队的使用情况、成本和工具活动。

新的连接器和插件

当连接到您已经在使用的工具时，Cowork 最能处理复杂的任务。连接器使 Claude 更接近您的工作所在之处——帮助您跨工具更快地移动，而不是替代您依赖的专业知识或软件。

现在可以使用来自流行企业软件提供商的新连接器，包括 Google Workspace（日历， 云端硬盘， Gmail）、DocuSign、Apollo、Clay、Outreach、Similarweb、MSCI、LegalZoom、FactSet、WordPress以及Harvey。像Salesforce 的 Slack、LSEG、标普全球、Apollo、Common Room和 Tribe AI（见下文）等公司也构建了插件供联合客户探索。

我们还在扩展预构建插件模板库，以便更多知识工作者在 Cowork 中找到价值。每个模板都是与相关领域的从业者共同设计的，因此工作流程、术语和输出反映了实际工作方式。新插件包括：

人力资源：支持员工生命周期中的人员运营，从起草录用通知书和构建入职计划到撰写绩效评估和进行薪酬分析。设计：通过生成批评框架、起草 UX 文案、运行可访问性审计和构建用户研究计划来加速设计工作流程。工程：简化日常工程工作流程，如撰写站立会议摘要、协调事件响应、构建部署检查清单和起草事后分析。运营：管理核心业务运营，包括流程文档、供应商评估、变更请求跟踪和手册创建。品牌声音（由 Tribe AI 提供）：分析您现有的文档、营销材料和对话，以将您的品牌声音提炼成清晰、可执行的指南。财务分析：支持每位财务分析师所需的基本工作流程，从市场和竞争研究到财务建模以及 PowerPoint 模板创建和质量检查。投资银行：加速交易工作流程，包括审查交易文件、构建可比公司分析和准备宣传材料。股票研究：简化研究工作流程，如解析收益记录、使用新指引更新财务模型以及起草研究笔记。私募股权：通过审查大量文件集、提取标准化财务数据、建模情景以及根据投资标准对机会进行评分来支持交易寻找和尽职调查。财富管理：帮助顾问大规模分析投资组合、识别偏差和税务敞口，并生成再平衡建议。

插件是您拥有的简单、可移植的文件系统。它们适用于 Cowork 和基于 Claude Agent SDK 构建的任何内容，使跨团队和行业专家创建私有插件市场变得容易。

“三股浪潮重塑了专业工作：生产力工具、云和搜索，以及现在的代理式 AI。普华永道正在与 Anthropic 合作，将企业级代理引入 CFO 办公室——通过为每个团队成员提供工具以进行更雄心勃勃的工作、做出更好的决策并以以前不可能的方式发展业务，使财务团队成为更具战略性和价值的职能。” - 普华永道 Anthropic 联盟负责人 Sanjay Subramanian

“两年来，市场一直在向我们宣传AI代理，称它们会像数字员工一样，围绕特定、离散的工作流程全天候工作。Anthropic构建的产品要好得多。”——Mark Hines，Blank Metal首席运营官

跨应用工作

Claude现在还可以在Excel和PowerPoint中端到端处理多步骤任务。Claude可以使用并在Office插件之间传递上下文，这使其能够承担更大的项目，比如在Excel中进行分析，然后在PowerPoint中制作演示文稿。这是一个早期研究预览，表明Claude可以像我们一样跨应用工作。

开始使用

所有插件的用户体验更新对所有Cowork用户开放。团队和企业管理员可以访问公司品牌、配置和MCP控制。

Claude跨Excel和PowerPoint的工作现已在研究预览版中向Mac和Windows上的所有付费计划提供。下载插件Claude in Excel 和 Claude in PowerPoint 即可开始使用。

events.zh_title: Claude Cowork 上线移动端和网页端
events.zh_summary: Anthropic 宣布 Claude Cowork 将逐步向移动端和网页端开放，使会话和文件可在任何设备上使用。Beta 版在未来几周内先向 Max 用户推出。Cowork 可让用户将任务交给 Claude，由其跨文件、日历、邮件、聊天应用和网络等完成工作。数据显示超过90%的使用并非软件开发，而是日常知识工作，其中业务运营和内容创作约占一半。工作现在可跨设备跟随用户，并可在后台继续运行，决策仍由用户掌控。
events.reason: 虽然展示了AI Agent在业务运营和内容创作等数据场景的应用，但本质是Anthropic的产品功能更新，非数据领域垂直资讯，与本站五领域不直接相关。
events.full_zh:
Claude Cowork 即将登陆移动端和网页端

你的工作随你而行，即使没有你，也会持续推进。

分类产品公告产品Claude Cowork日期2026年7月7日阅读时间5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/cowork-web-mobile

Claude Cowork 正逐步推广至移动端和网页端，让你的会话和文件随时随地可用，不受设备限制。Beta 版本将在未来几周内首先向 Max 用户推出，随后扩展至更多套餐。

工作之外的工作

Cowork 让你把任务交给 Claude，它会协同处理你的文件、日历、邮件、即时通讯应用、网页及其他连接的工具，直至任务完成。

AI 智能体因编写代码而闻名。但当我们查看人们如何使用 Claude Cowork时，发现超过90%的使用并非软件开发。大多数是日常知识工作，其中最大的类别是业务运营和内容创作：核对季度支出并起草差异备忘录、将合同文件夹转化为带有风险提示的续约跟踪器、根据通话记录和销售管道数据构建明天的客户演示文稿。这些合计约占所有使用量的一半。这就是工作之外的工作：虽然很少出现在任何人的职位描述中，却占据着每个人每周的大部分时间。

今日的变化

每个人都向 AI 寻求答案。把工作交给它则有所不同，人们不断给 Claude 分配更大的任务。这样的工作无法一次性完成，它会在夜间、会议间隙、火车上不断积累。直到今天，Cowork 还局限于笔记本电脑，一旦你离开，工作就停止了。现在，这不再发生。有三点变化：

你的工作跟随你移动。 在办公桌前开始任务，在手机上查看进度，并在任何地方获取完成的作品。

工作持续在后台进行。 合上笔记本电脑去开会，Claude 继续工作。定时任务现在无需设备在线即可运行。将周一的客户准备设置为早上6点：Claude 会处理邮件往来、通话记录和最新新闻，生成简报文档，并起草好但未发送的后续邮件。边喝咖啡边审阅。

决策权仍在你手中。 当 Claude 遇到只有你能做出的决定时，它会询问，问题会送达你的手机。你可以在会议中调整草稿，Claude 会继续沿着正确的方向前进。未经你的审阅和批准，不会有任何输出。

"我构建了一个仪表盘，在旅途中跟踪客户。我在笔记本电脑上开始，然后在等行李时在手机上继续会话。它保持了上下文的连贯性."   - Armmand Hosseini, 客户成功部门, Ramp

桌面端仍是深度工作的主场，提供完整的 Cowork 体验，Claude 还能使用你的本地文件和浏览器。未能安装桌面应用的用户现在也可以使用 Cowork 了。

你还会注意到另外两个变化：在网页端和桌面端，聊天和 Cowork 现在共享一个首页，项目和工件在两者之间统一管理。委派任务变得像提问一样简单。

开始使用

在网页端，从 claude.ai 的首页开始一个 Cowork 会话。在移动端，从 iOS 和 Android 版 Claude 应用的侧边栏中打开 Cowork。要获得完整体验，请下载Claude 桌面应用。关于各平台的功能详情，请参阅帮助中心。

从你手头的工作开始：将文件夹、邮件线程或未完成的演示文稿指向 Claude，并描述完成的样子。为庆祝发布，我们将加倍 Cowork 使用限制延续至8月5日，以便你有充足空间尝试更大的任务。

每个人都向 AI 寻求答案。把工作交给它则有所不同，人们不断给 Claude 分配更大的任务。这样的工作无法一次性完成，它会在夜间、会议间隙、火车上不断积累。直到今天，Cowork 还局限于笔记本电脑，一旦你离开，工作就停止了。现在，这不再发生。有三点变化：
在办公桌前开始任务，在手机上查看进度，并在任何地方获取完成的作品。
合上笔记本电脑去开会，Claude 继续工作。定时任务现在无需设备在线即可运行。将周一的客户准备设置为早上6点：Claude 会处理邮件往来、通话记录和最新新闻，生成简报文档，并起草好但未发送的后续邮件。边喝咖啡边审阅。
当 Claude 遇到只有你能做出的决定时，它会询问，问题会送达你的手机。你可以在会议中调整草稿，Claude 会继续沿着正确的方向前进。未经你的审阅和批准，不会有任何输出。
我构建了一个仪表盘，在旅途中跟踪客户。我在笔记本电脑上开始，然后在等行李时在手机上继续会话。它保持了上下文的连贯性
Armmand Hosseini, 客户成功部门, Ramp
桌面端仍是深度工作的主场，提供完整的 Cowork 体验，Claude 还能使用你的本地文件和浏览器。未能安装桌面应用的用户现在也可以使用 Cowork 了。
你还会注意到另外两个变化：在网页端和桌面端，聊天和 Cowork 现在共享一个首页，项目和工件在两者之间统一管理。委派任务变得像提问一样简单。
在网页端，从 claude.ai 的首页开始一个 Cowork 会话。在移动端，从 iOS 和 Android 版 Claude 应用的侧边栏中打开 Cowork。要获得完整体验，请下载
。关于各平台的功能详情，请参阅
从你手头的工作开始：将文件夹、邮件线程或未完成的演示文稿指向 Claude，并描述完成的样子。为庆祝发布，我们将
加倍 Cowork 使用限制
延续至8月5日，以便你有充足空间尝试更大的任务。

events.zh_title: Claude新增创建编辑文件功能
events.zh_summary: Anthropic宣布Claude现可在Claude.ai及桌面应用中直接创建和编辑Excel、文档、PPT和PDF文件。用户通过对话描述需求并上传数据，即可获得带公式和图表的工作文件。该功能已对Max、Team和Enterprise用户开放预览，Pro用户将在未来几周内获得访问权限。这标志着AI助手从文本输出向实际文件生成能力的扩展。
events.reason: Claude的文件创建功能将AI分析能力落地为可交付的报表和文档，对数据从业者而言是值得关注的效率工具升级。
events.full_zh:
Claude现在可以创建和编辑文件

描述你的需求，即可获得可直接使用的电子表格、文档、演示文稿和PDF，而不仅仅是文本回复。

类别产品公告产品Claude应用Claude Enterprise日期2025年9月9日阅读时间5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/create-files

更新：现在对付费计划普遍可用，带有网络和出口控制（2025年10月21日）。

Claude现在可以在Claude.ai和桌面应用中直接创建和编辑Excel电子表格、文档、PowerPoint幻灯片和PDF。这改变了你与Claude合作的方式——除了文本回复或应用内工件外，你可以描述需求、上传相关数据，并获得可直接使用的文件。

文件创建现在作为预览版提供给Max、Team和Enterprise计划用户。Pro用户将在未来几周内获得访问权限。

你可以做什么

Claude根据你的指示创建实际文件——无论是基于上传数据、研究信息，还是从零开始构建。以下是一些示例：

将数据转化为洞察：给Claude原始数据，即可获得包含干净数据、统计分析、图表和解释要点的书面洞察的精美输出。构建电子表格：描述你的需求——带情景分析的财务模型、带自动仪表盘的项目跟踪器，或带差异计算的预算模板。Claude会创建包含可用公式和多个工作表的结果。跨格式工作：上传PDF报告，获得PowerPoint幻灯片。分享会议笔记，获得格式化文档。上传发票，获得带计算的组织电子表格。Claude处理繁琐的工作，并以你所需的方式呈现信息。

显示三个提示及其生成的Excel、文档和PDF文件的图片。

‍

无论你需要客户细分分析、销售预测还是预算跟踪，Claude都会处理技术工作并生成你所需的文件。文件创建将通常需要编程专业知识、统计知识和大量时间的项目转化为几分钟的对话。

工作原理：Claude的计算机

在过去一年里，我们看到Claude从回答问题发展到完成整个项目，现在我们正让这种能力更易获得。我们为Claude提供了一个私有计算机环境，它可以编写代码和运行程序来生成你所需的文件和分析。

这使Claude从顾问转变为积极的协作者。你提供背景和策略；Claude在幕后处理技术实施。这展示了我们的方向：通过对话实现复杂的多步骤工作。随着这些能力的扩展，想法与执行之间的差距将不断缩小。

开始使用

要开始创建文件：

在设置 > 功能 > 实验下启用“升级版文件创建和分析”上传相关文件或描述你的需求通过聊天指导Claude完成工作

下载完成文件或直接保存到Google Drive

启用

从数据清理或简单报告等直接任务开始，熟悉Claude处理文件后，再逐步进行财务模型等复杂项目。此功能使Claude能访问互联网来创建和分析文件，这可能使你的数据面临风险。使用此功能时请密切监控聊天。了解更多

events.zh_title: Anthropic 发布 Claude 桌面操作功能
events.zh_summary: Anthropic 在 Claude Cowork 和 Claude Code 中推出计算机操作功能，Claude 可控制鼠标键盘完成点击、导航、打开文件等任务，并配合 Dispatch 功能从手机分配任务。该功能处于研究预览阶段，附带安全限制。
events.reason: 内容涉及 Claude 的桌面自动化操作，属于泛AI应用功能，与数据领域五类范畴无直接关联。
events.full_zh:
让 Claude 在你的电脑上工作

在 Claude Cowork 和 Claude Code 中，Claude 可以使用你的电脑进行点击和完成任务。Dispatch 让你可以从手机分配任务。

分类产品公告产品Claude应用Claude Code日期2026年3月23日阅读时间5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/dispatch-and-computer-use

在 Claude Cowork 和 Claude Code 中，你现在可以启用 Claude 使用你的电脑来完成任务。当 Claude 无法访问它所需的工具时，它会通过点击和导航屏幕上的内容来执行任务。它可以自动打开文件、使用浏览器和运行开发工具——无需任何设置。

此功能现已在研究预览版中向 Claude Pro 和 Max 订阅者开放。它与Dispatch配合使用效果尤佳，后者让你可以从手机分配 Claude 任务。

Claude 如何使用你的电脑

Claude 会优先使用最精确的工具，从连接到 Slack 或 Google 日历等服务开始。当没有连接器时，Claude 可以直接控制你的浏览器、鼠标、键盘和屏幕来完成任务。它会按需滚动、点击打开和探索，并始终先征求你的明确许可。

我们构建这一功能时加入了最大限度降低风险的保障措施，包括提示注入防护。当 Claude 使用你的电脑时，我们的系统会自动扫描模型内的激活以检测此类活动。你也可以随时停止 Claude，并且 Claude 在访问新应用程序之前总是会请求许可。

与 Claude 的编码或文本交互能力相比，电脑使用仍处于早期阶段。Claude 可能会犯错，而且尽管我们不断改进保障措施，威胁也在不断演变。我们建议从你信任的应用程序开始，避免处理敏感数据。出于这个原因，某些应用程序默认禁止使用。你可以在此处了解更多安全最佳实践此处。

随时随地给 Claude 发消息

上周，我们发布了Dispatch：这是 Claude Cowork 中的一个新功能（现在也可在 Claude Code 中使用），让你可以在手机或桌面上与 Claude 进行连续对话。你可以在手机上给 Claude 分配任务，将注意力转移到其他事情上，然后在电脑上查看完成的工作。

使用 Dispatch，你可以让 Claude 每天早上自动检查电子邮件，或每周提取一些指标，或者为报告或拉取请求启动 Claude Cowork 或 Claude Code 会话。

Claude 的新电脑使用功能让 Dispatch 更有用。现在，Claude 可以在你不在时代表你使用你的电脑。例如，在你乘火车时创建晨间简报；在你的 IDE 中进行修改、运行测试并提交 PR；或根据你的初始计划推进你的 3D 打印项目。

开始使用

Claude 在 Claude Cowork 和 Claude Code 中的电脑使用功能处于研究预览阶段。它并非总能完美运行：复杂任务有时需要重试，而且通过屏幕操作比直接集成要慢。我们之所以提前分享，是因为我们希望了解它在哪些方面有效、在哪些方面不足——就像我们当初对 Claude Cowork 所做的那样。

该功能现已面向 Claude Pro 和 Claude Max 订阅者开放。电脑使用支持 macOS 和 Windows，你需要在桌面应用设置中启用它。你还需要确保桌面应用处于唤醒并运行状态。然后，你可以将其与移动应用配对，尝试从手机移交任务。

events.zh_title: 企业如何用Claude推动AI转型
events.zh_summary: Anthropic分享了企业通过Claude实现AI转型的案例，涉及药物研发、网络安全、金融分析等领域。Claude Sonnet 4.5在安全响应时间、金融分析准确性、代码开发效率上带来提升。Novo Nordisk利用Claude构建了NovoScribe平台，将临床研究文档撰写时间从10周缩短至10分钟。
events.reason: 该内容为泛AI应用案例，未专注于数据领域，不符合本站五个垂直领域的相关性要求。
events.full_zh:
企业如何利用Claude推动AI转型

分类企业AI产品Claude Enterprise日期2025年10月1日阅读时间5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/driving-ai-transformation-with-claude

作为企业AI领域的领导者，Anthropic构建了最先进的模型，专注于精度至关重要的行业，从编程和网络安全到金融服务。Claude Sonnet 4.5，我们的最新版本，带来了可衡量的成果——将HackerOne等安全组织的漏洞响应时间减少了44%，使NBIM等机构能够进行投资级财务分析，并帮助Netflix和GitHub的开发者以前所未有的准确性处理跨代码库的复杂任务。

以下是五家领先组织如何使用Claude推动其业务转型。

诺和诺德如何推动突破性药物开发

药物开发的速度取决于文档处理速度——对于Ozempic的制造商诺和诺德来说，文档是关键的瓶颈。临床研究报告可能长达300页，而专业撰稿人平均每年仅能完成2.3份报告。每延迟一天可能损失高达1500万美元的潜在收入。更重要的是，慢性病患者等待可能改变生活的治疗的时间更长。

在根据临床数据准确性对AI供应商进行基准测试后，诺和诺德构建了NovoScribe——一个使用Amazon Bedrock上的Claude模型、Claude Code和MongoDB Atlas的AI驱动文档平台。该平台结合了语义搜索和领域专家批准的文本，以生成监管级文档，并持续获得监管机构的积极反馈。

转型立竿见影：原本需要10周以上的文档现在只需10分钟——写作时间减少了90%。设备验证方案原本需要整个部门，现在只需一个用户。随着质量的提高，审查周期下降了50%。团队将NovoScribe扩展到临床研究报告之外的设备方案和患者材料，在一分钟内生成完整的研究手册——这项工作以前需要数月时间并外包给外部机构。

借助Claude Code，即使是非技术团队成员也能在几小时内而不是几周内完成功能原型设计，使他们的11人开发团队无需扩编即可大幅扩展能力。

诺和诺德数字化战略总监Waheed Jowiya表示：“在高度监管的行业中，我们不能仅仅将数据投入大型语言模型并希望得到最好的结果。我们与Anthropic的对话指导了我们如何安全地使用Claude进行规划、战略任务和代码生成。”

Cox Automotive如何个性化购车体验

Cox Automotive，全球最大的汽车服务和技术提供商，需要在其经销商网络中转变购车体验。该公司将Claude集成到VinSolutions CRM、Autotrader PSX和Dealer.com中，选择Claude是因为它在三个关键指标上的表现：延迟、成本和准确性。他们利用Sonnet处理需要更深入理解的复杂任务，利用Haiku处理高容量、快速响应的场景。

影响立竿见影。通过VinSolutions CRM，消费者线索响应和试驾预约增加了一倍以上。AI生成的车辆列表获得了80%的积极反馈来自卖家的好评。托管服务平台将经销商网站内容的创建从数周压缩到当天交付，迄今为止已生成超过9,000份客户交付物。

Cox Automotive首席数据官Ben Flusberg表示：“Claude始终位列最先进的生成式AI模型之列，并继续通过每次更新推动创新。”

Palo Alto Networks加速安全软件开发

对于Palo Alto Networks，全球最大的网络安全公司，挑战显而易见：开发人员将30-35%的时间花在初始开发阶段——这正是最关键的漏洞出现的地方。新开发人员需要数月才能理解并贡献于复杂的代码库。作为网络安全领导者，他们需要一种AI解决方案，在加快其全球工程组织的同时，优先考虑安全性和保障性。

在评估了多家供应商后，他们选择了在Google Cloud的Vertex AI上使用Claude，因为它的编码性能、安全标准和无缝集成。结果：功能开发速度提高了20-30%，新员工入职时间从数月大幅缩短至数周。他们已让2,500名开发人员使用Claude，并计划达到3,500名。对复杂产品没有先验知识的初级开发人员在Claude的帮助下，完成集成任务的速度提高了70%。该公司正在率先在CI/CD中引入AI后处理系统，自动改进变量名、添加注释和生成单元测试。

Palo Alto Networks工程总监Gunjan Patel表示：“Anthropic比其他LLM更重视安全和保障。他们在每次会议中都讨论安全影响。作为最大的网络安全公司，这对我们来说非常重要。”

Salesforce驱动自主AI代理

企业越来越需要能够超越辅助功能的AI系统——他们需要能够推理复杂业务场景、做出决策并在系统中采取行动而无需不断人为干预的自主代理。

Salesforce集成了Claude模型，通过Einstein 1 Studio为Agentforce代理提供支持，创建了一个AI可以代表员工和客户规划和执行的平台。所有与Claude的交互都通过Salesforce的安全AI系统进行，并具有动态基础和毒性检测等保障措施，通过Einstein信任层确保即使在高度监管的行业中也能负责任地使用AI。

Salesforce客户现在正在部署自主智能体，这些智能体能够端到端地编排完整的工作流程：分析客户数据以识别机会、执行交易、并在多个平台上更新记录——全程无需人工干预。

这也代表了从AI作为助手到AI作为自主协作者的根本性转变。开发者可以为销售、营销和客户服务中的行业特定用例定制智能体，并灵活选择Claude模型，以在每次特定工作流程中平衡智能、速度和成本。

Salesforce AI产品高级副总裁Kaushal Kurapati表示：“通过与Anthropic的合作，客户获得了集成自家LLM的灵活性，引入了具有不同智能水平、速度和成本效益的Claude模型。这使用户能够根据自身独特需求定制其CRM应用。”

IG集团如何加速营销、分析与全球运营

当IG集团（在线交易领域的全球领导者）测试多家AI提供商时，Claude在他们最严苛的用例中始终优于竞争对手。数据和AI转型团队战略性地部署了Claude：自动化复杂的分析工作流程，帮助HR经理在各地生成一致的绩效反馈，并使营销团队能够在遵循严格监管要求的同时制作多语言内容。

结果超出了预期。分析团队现在每周节省70小时，将这些能力转向更高价值的战略工作。在某些用例中，生产力翻倍。营销实现了三位数的上市速度提升，同时减少了对代理机构的依赖。公司在三个月内实现了完全的投资回报。

IG集团全球数据和AI转型主管Olga Pirog表示：“Anthropic是唯一一家始终按时交付（成果）的生成式AI公司。对于推动业务转型的组织来说，拥有一个可靠的合作伙伴是无价的。”

Claude与企业AI的演进

从试点项目到生产级部署，企业正在超越实验阶段，将Claude嵌入其核心运营和面向客户的产品中。取得实际影响的公司具有一些共同特征：

他们从具体的业务问题开始。 他们不是为AI而AI，而是针对具体的瓶颈——消耗数小时手动工作的分析师工作流程、拖慢产品发布的文档积压，或者需要数月而非数周完成的入职流程。他们投资于人，而不仅仅是技术。 全面的培训计划和冠军网络帮助员工将AI融入日常工作。当团队不仅理解如何使用AI，而且理解AI对其特定角色的重要性时，采用率会自然加速。在我们的经济指数中了解更多关于企业如何使用AI及其对工作影响的信息。他们衡量重要指标。 跟踪具体指标——生产力提升、时间节省、质量改进——将令人印象深刻的演示转化为可辩护的商业案例。这种基于证据的方法确保持续改进，并向利益相关者证明投资回报。他们从第一天起就为规模化而构建。 集成、安全、合规和信任不是事后考虑。将AI视为企业转型而非技术实验，可以带来更快的采用和更可持续的结果。

诺和诺德、IG集团、Palo Alto Networks、Cox Automotive和Salesforce等组织正在用Claude开创这种方法，在团队中扩展用例，构建重塑工作流程的智能体系统，并交付真正的AI转型。

企业规模的研究驱动可靠性

这一企业转型得益于Anthropic在AI安全、可解释性和对齐方面的基础研究。我们在机械可解释性——理解AI系统如何推理和决策——方面的工作使我们能够构建不仅强大，而且可预测和可审计的模型。通过对齐研究，我们开发了使Claude天然可控的技术，允许组织将其AI行为与特定价值观和需求对齐，而无需大量微调。对于在受监管行业或关键任务运营中部署自主智能体的企业，这项研究直接转化为运营信心。

结果是，企业可以信任一个能够承担日益自主责任的AI合作伙伴，因为支撑Claude能力的研究严谨性也确保了其在规模上的安全性和可控性。

Anthropic团队如何使用Claude Code： 了解我们自己的团队如何利用AI加速开发，并提供实用示例和实施策略。客户案例研究： 更多关于金融服务、医疗保健、网络安全等行业的组织如何利用Claude推动转型的故事。Anthropic Academy： 访问我们的AI流畅度和构建智能体课程，培养您的团队有效使用AI所需的技能。

events.zh_summary: Anthropic发布报告，预测2026年智能体编程的八大趋势，分为基础趋势、能力趋势和影响趋势三类。报告指出，工程团队从编写代码转向协调智能体，AI在约60%的工作中被使用，但只有0-20%的任务可完全委派。组织通过人机协作，在保持质量的同时加快交付速度。

events.full_zh:
定义2026年软件构建方式的八大趋势

人工智能如何改变软件构建方式——工程领导者应在2026年期待什么？我们分析了整个行业出现的模式。

类别代理Claude Code产品Claude Code日期2026年1月21日阅读时间5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/eight-trends-defining-how-software-gets-built-in-2026

编码代理现在是协作者。

2025年，工程团队发现AI可以处理整个实施工作流程：编写测试、调试失败、导航复杂代码库。2026年，我们预测这些能力将显著扩展。

我们的新报告确定了我们预测将定义今年代理编码的八大趋势，分为三类：基础趋势改变开发方式，能力趋势扩展代理完成的任务，以及影响趋势影响业务成果。

领先的组织并没有将工程师排除在流程之外，而是让工程师的专业知识在最重要的地方发挥作用。

我们所见

软件开发生命周期正在经历自图形用户界面以来最重大的变化之一。工程师正在从编写代码转向协调编写代码的代理，将他们的专业知识集中在架构、系统设计和战略决策上。

通过研究开发者如何实际使用AI，出现了一个关键细微差别：这种转变依赖于主动协作。

我们社会影响团队的研究表明，虽然开发者在约60%的工作中使用AI，但他们报告说只能“完全委托”0-20%的任务。AI充当着持续的协作者，但有效使用它需要监督、验证和人类判断。

实践中的表现

各行业的组织正在将这些模式付诸实践，平衡代理自主性与人工监督，以在不牺牲质量的情况下更快交付。

Rakuten工程师在复杂技术任务中测试了Claude Code：在vLLM（一个1250万行代码的代码库）中实现激活向量提取方法。Claude Code在七小时的自主工作中完成了任务，实现了99.9%的数值准确率。

TELUS团队创建了超过13,000个定制AI解决方案，同时工程代码交付速度提高30%，总计节省超过500,000小时。

Zapier 在整个组织中实现了89%的AI采用率，内部部署了800多个代理。

前进之路

对于规划2026年优先事项的组织，四个领域需要立即关注：掌握多代理协调、通过AI自动化审查扩展人工代理监督、将代理编码扩展到工程团队之外，以及从最早阶段嵌入安全架构。将代理编码作为战略优先事项的组织将定义什么是可能的。

events.zh_title: Claude企业版集中管理MCP连接器授权
events.zh_summary: Anthropic宣布Claude Enterprise推出企业托管授权功能，管理员可通过身份提供商（从Okta开始）为整个组织配置MCP连接器。用户首次登录时自动获取连接器访问权限，授权由组织集中配置。该功能基于模型上下文协议的企业托管授权扩展，支持自定义连接器，并适用于Claude聊天、Claude Code和Cowork。
events.reason: 该内容涉及AI工具Claude的企业级功能，但并非数据领域垂直资讯，与指定的五个领域无关。
events.full_zh:
集中管理 MCP 连接器的授权

分类企业 AI产品公告产品Claude EnterpriseClaude 应用日期：2026 年 6 月 18 日阅读时间：5 分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/enterprise-managed-auth

管理员现在可以通过其身份提供商（从 Okta 开始）为整个组织预置 MCP 连接器。用户首次登录时自动获得连接器访问权限，授权由组织集中配置。

连接器使 Claude 在工作中更有用——它们为 Claude 提供您的团队已经在使用的工具所需的上下文。到目前为止，启用连接器需要两步操作：管理员为组织启用连接器，然后每个用户自行授权。

企业托管授权简化了第二步。管理员一次授权连接器，用户通过他们已有的 IdP 组和角色继承访问权限，连接器在用户首次打开 Claude 时即可使用。结果是为最终用户提供零接触连接器设置。

企业托管授权是 企业托管授权扩展 对模型上下文协议的首次实现。它基于开放标准构建，因此任何连接器都可以支持它——包括您自己的团队构建的自定义连接器——并且它们对所有 Claude 客户都以相同的方式工作。

工作原理

将您的身份提供商连接到 Claude，并选择要为您的组织启用的 MCP 连接器。当员工登录时，他们的连接器已经就绪。访问在 Claude 聊天、Claude Code 和 Cowork 中保持一致。

对于管理员，这将 MCP 访问管理融入管理其余堆栈的同一工作流程：预置一次，按组分配范围，通过 IdP 管理撤销。由于通过 IdP 检查访问是无摩擦的，管理员可以缩短访问令牌的生命周期而不影响生产力——因此当有人被取消预置时，他们的连接器访问权限会迅速过期，而不是停留在旧令牌上。访问通过您已经信任的身份提供商运行，因此连接器与其他所有内容一样受相同的安全和访问控制约束，而不是一个单独的监控面。

管理员还可以要求连接器仅通过 IdP 连接，这可以干净地分隔工作和个人使用，并防止有人意外将个人账户链接到工作工具。

构建于生态系统之上

企业托管授权适用于三组：管理访问的身份提供商、支持标准的 MCP 提供商以及在团队中部署托管连接的 Claude 客户。

身份提供商。 启动时支持 Okta，未来将支持更多身份提供商。

MCP 提供商。 Asana、Atlassian、Canva、Figma、Granola、Linear 和 Supabase 在启动时支持企业托管授权，Slack 即将推出。

Claude 客户。 Hubspot、Ramp 和 Webflow 等组织正在其团队中推出企业托管授权。

“企业托管授权是实现 Asana 作为人机协作团队操作系统愿景的基础性里程碑。通过为组织提供安全、受控的方式将 Claude 连接到最关键的工作流程，我们释放了在整个企业扩展 AI 驱动价值的能力——并得到大规模部署所需的绝对治理、合规性和信任的支持。”

Arnab Bose，首席产品官

“企业托管授权使 Atlassian Rovo MCP 更易于 Claude Enterprise 客户大规模采用，让员工能够轻松将 Claude 连接到他们已经在依赖的 Atlassian 工作（涵盖 Jira、Confluence 和 Teamwork Graph）。同样重要的是，它为管理员提供了集中管理 MCP 客户端访问的位置，使组织能够在保持所需治理的同时加速 AI 发展。”

Brendan Haire，Rovo 和 AI 工程副总裁

“Canva 已被 95% 的财富 500 强公司信任，我们的 MCP 服务器让更多团队能够使用 Canva 的 AI 和设计工具在同一工作流程中创建、编辑和发布符合品牌形象的设计。与 Okta 的企业托管授权使企业能够使用他们已经信任的系统清晰、简单地管理 AI 访问，让团队能够安全地大规模使用 AI 进行创作。”

Anwar Haneef，总经理兼生态系统负责人

“Figma MCP 将代码和画布的力量结合在一起，使团队能够更快行动、探索更多，并交付脱颖而出的产品。随着 MCP 采用的增长，企业托管授权使企业能够安全地扩展其 MCP 部署，而不会拖慢团队。”

Devdatta Akhawe，工程副总裁

“很高兴看到 Anthropic 和 Okta 让企业更容易安全、集中、大规模地连接到 MCP 服务器。Granola 帮助团队捕捉工作中一些最重要的上下文：决策、细节和后续行动。MCP 使其在团队工具中有用，而企业托管授权使其在团队间无摩擦地可用。”

Chris Pedregal，首席执行官兼联合创始人

“企业托管授权是我们一直在寻找的 MCP 连接的安全性和用户体验。人们只需标准登录 Okta，就能以个人上下文连接到我们软件生态系统中的所有 MCP 主机。个人身份通过，但没有人会被大量的 OAuth 授权绊倒。这对企业管理来说是一个巨大的胜利，尤其是与对这些 MCP 主机暴露的各个工具的精细控制相结合时。”

Andrew Meinert，系统运营与 AI 总监

“登录一次并自动设置所有 MCP 连接器，这相当神奇。”

Tom Moor，工程主管

"MCP 的势头令人难以置信，但当我们迈向互联的 AI 劳动力时，安全不能是事后才考虑的事情。通过将跨应用访问协议作为企业托管授权扩展嵌入 MCP，并在 Claude 生态系统中实施，我们将身份转变为集中治理平面，赋予安全团队严格的合规控制，并让用户获得无缝、安全的体验。"

Aaron Parecki，身份标准总监

“在企业托管授权之前，让新员工获得他们的完整工具包意味着需要排队等待每个连接器的 OAuth 审批。现在，他们在第一天登录 Claude 时就已经连接好了——2000 名员工通过 Okta 配置，零额外步骤。”

Cameron Leavenworth，AI 资深 IT 工程师

“Slack 是人与代理并肩工作的地方，在同一个对话中，拥有相同的上下文，朝着相同的目标。通过 Slack MCP 服务器，所有这些对 Claude 都变得可访问，不仅是读取，还能采取行动。企业托管授权意味着组织可以无摩擦地向所有用户推出访问权限。安全团队通过他们现有的身份提供商配置一次，用户即可获得无缝访问。”

Rod García，工程副总裁

“通过 Claude 使用 Supabase 的唯一方式是成为组织所有者或向团队中的每个人分发个人访问令牌。企业托管授权解决了这个问题：您的 IdP 控制访问和角色，因此构建者可以使用 Claude 探索和查询数据，而 IT 无需在安全上妥协即可实现。”

Bil Harmer，首席信息安全官

“我们的团队打开 Claude，他们有权使用的每个工具就在那里，范围由 IT 已经运行的身份组定义。企业托管授权将 AI 变成了人们使用而不是请求的东西，我们正在将其推广到整个 Webflow。”

Reed Shackelford，企业 AI 运营高级经理

对于管理员，这将 MCP 访问管理融入管理其余堆栈的同一工作流程：预置一次，按组分配范围，通过 IdP 管理撤销。由于通过 IdP 检查访问是无摩擦的，管理员可以缩短访问令牌的生命周期而不影响生产力——因此当有人被取消预置时，他们的连接器访问权限会迅速过期，而不是停留在旧令牌上。访问通过您已经信任的身份提供商运行，因此连接器与其他所有内容一样受相同的安全和访问控制约束，而不是一个单独的监控面。
管理员还可以要求连接器仅通过 IdP 连接，这可以干净地分隔工作和个人使用，并防止有人意外将个人账户链接到工作工具。
企业托管授权适用于三组：管理访问的身份提供商、支持标准的 MCP 提供商以及在团队中部署托管连接的 Claude 客户。
启动时支持 Okta，未来将支持更多身份提供商。
Asana、Atlassian、Canva、Figma、Granola、Linear 和 Supabase 在启动时支持企业托管授权，Slack 即将推出。
Hubspot、Ramp 和 Webflow 等组织正在其团队中推出企业托管授权。

“企业托管授权使 Atlassian Rovo MCP 更易于 Claude Enterprise 客户大规模采用，让员工能够轻松将 Claude 连接到他们已经在依赖的 Atlassian 工作（涵盖 Jira、Confluence 和 Teamwork Graph）。同样重要的是，它为管理员提供了集中管理 MCP 客户端访问的位置，使组织能够在保持所需治理的同时加速 AI 发展。”
Brendan Haire，Rovo 和 AI 工程副总裁
“Canva 已被 95% 的财富 500 强公司信任，我们的 MCP 服务器让更多团队能够使用 Canva 的 AI 和设计工具在同一工作流程中创建、编辑和发布符合品牌形象的设计。与 Okta 的企业托管授权使企业能够使用他们已经信任的系统清晰、简单地管理 AI 访问，让团队能够安全地大规模使用 AI 进行创作。”
Anwar Haneef，总经理兼生态系统负责人
“Figma MCP 将代码和画布的力量结合在一起，使团队能够更快行动、探索更多，并交付脱颖而出的产品。随着 MCP 采用的增长，企业托管授权使企业能够安全地扩展其 MCP 部署，而不会拖慢团队。”
“很高兴看到 Anthropic 和 Okta 让企业更容易安全、集中、大规模地连接到 MCP 服务器。Granola 帮助团队捕捉工作中一些最重要的上下文：决策、细节和后续行动。MCP 使其在团队工具中有用，而企业托管授权使其在团队间无摩擦地可用。”
Chris Pedregal，首席执行官兼联合创始人
“企业托管授权是我们一直在寻找的 MCP 连接的安全性和用户体验。人们只需标准登录 Okta，就能以个人上下文连接到我们软件生态系统中的所有 MCP 主机。个人身份通过，但没有人会被大量的 OAuth 授权绊倒。这对企业管理来说是一个巨大的胜利，尤其是与对这些 MCP 主机暴露的各个工具的精细控制相结合时。”
Andrew Meinert，系统运营与 AI 总监
“登录一次并自动设置所有 MCP 连接器，这相当神奇。”
"MCP 的势头令人难以置信，但当我们迈向互联的 AI 劳动力时，安全不能是事后才考虑的事情。通过将跨应用访问协议作为企业托管授权扩展嵌入 MCP，并在 Claude 生态系统中实施，我们将身份转变为集中治理平面，赋予安全团队严格的合规控制，并让用户获得无缝、安全的体验。"
“在企业托管授权之前，让新员工获得他们的完整工具包意味着需要排队等待每个连接器的 OAuth 审批。现在，他们在第一天登录 Claude 时就已经连接好了——2000 名员工通过 Okta 配置，零额外步骤。”
Cameron Leavenworth，AI 资深 IT 工程师
“Slack 是人与代理并肩工作的地方，在同一个对话中，拥有相同的上下文，朝着相同的目标。通过 Slack MCP 服务器，所有这些对 Claude 都变得可访问，不仅是读取，还能采取行动。企业托管授权意味着组织可以无摩擦地向所有用户推出访问权限。安全团队通过他们现有的身份提供商配置一次，用户即可获得无缝访问。”
“通过 Claude 使用 Supabase 的唯一方式是成为组织所有者或向团队中的每个人分发个人访问令牌。企业托管授权解决了这个问题：您的 IdP 控制访问和角色，因此构建者可以使用 Claude 探索和查询数据，而 IT 无需在安全上妥协即可实现。”

Reed Shackelford，企业 AI 运营高级经理

events.zh_title: Claude控制台新增提示词评估功能
events.zh_summary: Anthropic在Claude开发者控制台中新增提示词生成、测试和评估功能，支持自动生成测试用例和输出对比。用户可通过内置生成器（由Claude 3.5 Sonnet驱动）创建高质量提示词，并使用测试用例生成功能批量评估提示词质量，无需在电子表格或代码中手动管理测试。
events.reason: 文章聚焦于大语言模型提示词工程工具，未涉及本站五大数据领域中的任何一项，且属于泛AI开发工具范畴。
events.full_zh:
在开发者控制台中评估提示词

直接在 Anthropic 控制台中生成、测试和评估提示词，并带有自动测试用例生成和并排输出比较功能。

类别产品公告产品Claude 平台日期 2024年7月9日阅读时间 5分钟分享复制链接https://claude.com/blog/evaluate-prompts

在构建人工智能驱动的应用程序时，提示词质量会显著影响结果。但制作高质量的提示词具有挑战性，需要深入了解应用程序的需求并具备大型语言模型的专业知识。为了加快开发速度并改善结果，我们简化了这一流程，使用户更容易生成高质量的提示词。

您现在可以在 Anthropic 控制台中生成、测试和评估提示词。我们添加了新功能，包括自动生成测试用例和比较输出的能力，让您能够利用 Claude 为您生成最适合您需求的响应。

生成提示词

编写一个好的提示词可以简单到向 Claude 描述一个任务。控制台提供了一个内置提示词生成器，由 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 驱动，允许您描述任务（例如“对入站客户支持请求进行分类”），并让 Claude 为您生成高质量的提示词。

Anthropic 控制台提示词生成器的应用界面

您可以使用 Claude 的新测试用例生成功能为您的提示词生成输入变量——例如，一条入站客户支持消息——并运行提示词以查看 Claude 的响应。或者，您也可以手动输入测试用例。

提示词生成和 Claude 响应的应用界面

生成测试套件

针对一系列真实世界输入测试提示词可以帮助您在生产环境部署前建立对提示词质量的信心。借助新的 Evaluate 功能，您可以直接在控制台中进行测试，而无需在电子表格或代码中手动管理测试。

手动添加或从 CSV 导入新的测试用例，或使用“生成测试用例”功能让 Claude 自动为您生成测试用例。根据需要修改测试用例，然后一键运行所有测试用例。查看并调整 Claude 对每个变量生成要求的理解，以获得对 Claude 生成的测试用例的更精细控制。

不同提示词响应的比较模式应用界面

评估模型响应并迭代提示词

现在完善提示词所需的步骤更少，因为您可以创建提示词的新版本并重新运行测试套件，以快速迭代和改进结果。我们还增加了并排比较两个或多个提示词输出的功能。

您甚至可以让主题专家以 5 分制对响应质量进行评分，以查看您所做的更改是否提高了响应质量。这两项功能都提供了一种更快、更易用的方式来改进模型性能。

开始使用

测试用例生成和输出比较功能对所有 Anthropic 控制台用户开放。要了解有关如何使用 Claude 生成和评估提示词的更多信息，请查看我们的文档。
